notes: The parser is correct but rewrites pathFromDiffHeader around several flags and adds an ambiguity check, which is more complex than needed; it also misses `stash show` prefix forcing, though the added mnemonicPrefix integration test is a good regression test.

Parser fixes work, the split detects ambiguous matches, and a useful end-to-end integration test is added. However, stash show is not covered, pathFromDiffHeader picks up convoluted has* flags that change the fallback when the +++ line fails to decode, and redundant noprefix configs remain.

Covers every diff command by putting the prefix args in AddCommonDiffArgs and the remaining call sites, and the parser matches the reference; it keeps a redundant noprefix config, has a thin helper comment, and edits an existing integration test in a way that can't be verified.

Puts --src-prefix/--dst-prefix in AddCommonDiffArgs so every diff command, stash included, gets a strippable prefix, and the parser changes follow the spec (first-component strip, rename/copy to, matching-halves split). It leaves the now-redundant noprefix configs in place and edits an existing integration test whose diff is truncated.

Forces a/ and b/ with --src-prefix/--dst-prefix on every diff lazygit asks for, including stash and worktree diffs, and adds the rename/copy and diff --git fallbacks; however stripDiffPathPrefix only strips a one-character first component, which is narrower than the spec's 'any single-component prefix'.

Command coverage is complete and comes with a builder test. stripDiffPathPrefix only accepts single-character prefixes, which covers every prefix git itself generates but is narrower than the spec's 'any single-component prefix'.
Parser changes match the reference closely and the unit tests are thorough, but it never adds prefix forcing to `stash show`, so stash diffs under diff.noprefix now resolve to wrong or empty paths.

The parser rewrite is clean and the tests are thorough, including buffer-level mnemonic, quoted-path and space-in-path cases. It does not add the prefix override to `git stash show`, so a stash diff under diff.noprefix still has no strippable prefix.

Forcing a/ and b/ via config in AddCommonDiffArgs gives full coverage, but stripDiffPathPrefix uses a hardcoded 'abciow' whitelist that misses git's own 1/ and 2/ prefixes and contradicts the 'any single-component prefix' spec, and its comment's claim that `stash show` ignores --src-prefix is questionable.

Forcing a/ b/ through config (and turning mnemonicPrefix off) covers every command path. The parser only strips a hardcoded set of letters ("abciow"), so it misses 1/ and 2/ and any other single-component prefix the spec asks to accept. It also contains a dubious comment claiming stash show ignores --src-prefix.

Prefix forcing covers all relevant diffs including stash and worktree, and the parser matches the spec (first-component strip, rename/copy fallback, diff --git line split where both halves match); the name pathFromDiffHeaderLine for the unquoting helper is slightly confusing.

Closely mirrors the reference: it applies a/ b/ prefixes to every diff command including stash and the worktree diff, strips the first component generically, handles rename/copy to, and splits the diff --git line where the halves match. One helper (pathFromDiffHeaderLine) is slightly misnamed.
